recommended_steps.detail: Editing usability through a consumer stays open for the user; deterministic proofs do not close it.
recommended_steps.title: Try editing mirrors through a consumer

recommended_steps.detail: The next phase replaces the shelf-wide mirror classification kept in this unreleased checkpoint and moves indexing coordination into one Biblios core; no release until that, the bounded import and the published Palace adoption land.
recommended_steps.title: One-core indexing phase next

see_for_yourself.expected: Reconcile re-indexes the edit without converting, the edited text is found by search, and the mirror file is unchanged.
steps: Run ./bin/python project/examples/shelf_demo.py on a scratch directory with two text files.
Edit one file under shelf/mirror/, then run reconcile again.
see_for_yourself.title: Edit a mirror and re-index it

what_just_landed.detail: An edited mirror is re-indexed from its own bytes, never re-converted or rewritten; one validated update call is the edit seam, and nothing on the ordinary path deletes mirror bytes.
what_just_landed.title: Mirrors belong to the user

what_just_landed.detail: Replacing a file converts the new bytes and keeps the previous mirror, including an unindexed edit, under a retained name with a provenance record.
what_just_landed.title: Replacement keeps the previous mirror

what_just_landed.detail: A missing, unreadable or malformed mirror isolates only its own entry; search, finish and checkpoint continue for the rest, and status names the problem.
what_just_landed.title: One bad mirror never blocks the shelf
